rubric_notes: Correctly places core histones, archaeal histones, TAFs and bacterial histone-fold proteins in a.22.1 (2.08), distinguishes class/fold/superfamily/family semantics, states superfamily = probable common ancestry, and explicitly refuses to transfer nucleosome or chromatin function to TAF or bacterial members. Name-only matches (H1 a.4.5.13, Dot1l c.66.1.31, HDAC c.42.1.2) correctly excluded and supported by its search evidence. Factual imprecision: states the superfamily has four families, omitting a.22.1.0 automated matches although its own a.22.1 search shows a.22.1.0 domains; human TAF number mappings (TAF(II)18/TAF10, TAF(II)28/TAF13) are off but are background, not SCOPe facts. Flat 'not evolutionarily related' for different-fold enzymes is a mild overstatement of what SCOPe asserts. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families a.204.1.2 / a.204.1.4, superfamily a.204.1 all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases, protein and species names, 7-93 boundary. Interprets as remote homology (common ancestor) not family-level and not fold-only; explicitly rejects assigning HisE/PRA-PH or MazG NTP pyrophosphohydrolase activity, pathway, mechanism, template use. Family names and protein names exceed the resolve-only bundle but are correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Families c.55.1.1, c.55.1.3, c.55.1.4 within c.55.1, fold c.55, class c and the additional families are all supported by the children listing and sccs search in the bundle. Superfamily correctly interpreted as remote homology with conserved ATP-binding two-lobe core; explicitly rejects transfer of substrate, mechanism, cellular role, catalytic residues, regulation, oligomeric state and ligand details, and rejects cross-family templates; fold-level c.55 described as purely structural. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Hierarchy, family SUNIDs, protein nodes (R2 47257, Mn catalase 47263), R1 subunit placements (a.98.1.1, c.7.1.2), and release dates are all supported by the bundle. Correct remote-homology/divergence interpretation, explicit refusal to transfer function/metal/mechanism/assembly, states that function calls need conserved metal ligands, family membership, close homologs and biochemical data, and usefully bounds the homology to the R2 subunit only. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct b.6.1.1/b.6.1.5/b.6.1.6 under b.6.1 in b.6, with sibling families and protein node 110108 supported by bundle. Treats superfamily as distant, probable common ancestry; rejects copper/electron-transfer inference, names required evidence (ligand residues plus metal-binding assays, spectroscopy, Cu-bound structure), and distinguishes fold-level modelling from functional templating. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families, superfamily, fold, class and sunids, bundle-supported; release facts supported. Distant homology via superfamily explained, family vs superfamily distinction clear, functional roles flagged as background knowledge; rejects conjugation, Ras, p97 and residue-level transfers and demands family/protein-level plus experimental evidence.

Correct and supported placements (c, c.23/52171, c.23.1/52172, c.23.1.1/52173, c.23.1.4/52252/52253, c.23.1.5/82344/82346, d1r8ja2, d1r8ja1 a.186.1.1); periodic-update label supported by /releases. Reasoning: superfamily implies common ancestry with low sequence identity, family-level relatedness not claimed; rejects phosphorelay/receiver function, catalysis, circadian transfer in both directions, template/active-site transfer, and warns against using the CheY family as the functional definition of the superfamily (addresses must_avoid). Names c.67.1.5 and d.125.1.1 correctly but also asserts a 'TIM-barrel-like portion' of ODC in a different fold, which does not exist in the Lactobacillus ODC that carries the wing; noncentral imprecision. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy, sunids and sibling superfamilies supported by bundle. Clearly frames the placement as asymmetric: homology asserted within b.84.5/b.84.5.1 (V- and A-type bulge domains), only fold-level similarity relative to b.84.1-b.84.4, neither asserting nor ruling out a shared ancestor. Rejects function, template and phylogeny inference from fold alone and notes release dependence. All must_include met. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Identifiers (f.21, f.21.1/81342, f.21.2/81343, f.21.3/103501, class f, release 2.08) supported by the bundle. Good fold/superfamily/family distinction, transfer rejected, needed evidence named (sequence profiles, conserved heme ligands, structural alignment, complex context). Calibration is weaker: it describes the groups as 'fold-level analogs' and frames the resemblance as fold-level or convergent without noting that separate superfamilies do not rule out undetectably distant homology. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families and sunids; Kch/MthK and succinyl-CoA synthetase alpha N-terminal domain (sunid 51901) supported by search bundles. Interpretation complete: remote homology at superfamily level, divergence, no transfer of ligand/catalysis/regulation, separate catalytic domain, per-family representatives, external evidence required. Noncentral factual error: states fold c.2 'also contains other superfamilies', but in SCOPe 2.08 c.2 contains only c.2.1. Release/periodic-update statement not in its own bundle but accurate. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct shared family k.40.1.1 (sunid 100905), superfamily 100904, protein and species sunids, and a calibrated reading that the shared family does not establish natural ancestry with good transfer limits. However the 'not a true family' annotation on the family node is never retrieved or mentioned; the caveat is inferred only from class k. Bio ceiling 2 for ignoring the decisive annotation; factual 2 for the missing material annotation.

Current 2.08 state correct (c.23.14 shared; c.23.14.1 vs c.23.14.2; d1t1ja1 used as current SID) and the unrelated-to-remote-homolog interpretation with function-transfer caveat is made. 1.69 side is vague recollection ('different fold or superfamily'); never states the c.137.1.1 own-fold placement of d1t1ja_. Falsely claims the API shows only the current state although its own /api/v1/releases evidence lists 1.69. Does not claim a shared superfamily in 1.69.

Correct d1a14h2 H:1-8 sunid 343393 l.1.1.1 with full class l lineage and sunids 310894/311501; d1a14h1 9-111 sunid 20061 b.1.1.1 V-set; d1a14l_ b.1.1.1 and d1a14n_ b.68.1.1 also correct. Bundle only contains the releases list, so lineage is not bundle-supported, but all stated facts are accurate and none fabricated. Clear rejection of tag similarity as homology with explanation of Synthetic label and short-segment information content, plus guidance to mask tags. Complete.

Complete and correct: 2.01 to 2.03 single d1acca_, split first in 2.04 and unchanged through 2.08, correct two-class classifications. Clear module reasoning, superfamily-vs-fold distinctions, limited function transfer, and release-specific search advice.

Identifiers, boundaries and sccs all correct; new fold d.394 identified; mosaic inference and function-transfer caveats present; extra 4i43 Jab1/MPN c.97.3.1 fact is supported by the bundle. Mischaracterizes the bromodomain relationship as 'distant' and 'more remote' when it is the only family-level (closest) placement among the five, and counts only three domains as related to previously characterized proteins. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Correct family and repeat-count reasoning with sensible limits. Claims PthA node 267645 and family-node parentage for d2kq5a_ and d4cj9a_ that are not in its bundle (only two search hits and a species node). Omits the 're' flag, 'single repeat' and canonical repeat unit; admits lengths come from background knowledge.

Correct metadata (2.08, 2.08-stable, dates, periodic 2.08-2026-08-16; bundle-supported, releases list also consistent). Cites stable release for reproducibility, adds dated periodic label when a periodic update was used, explicitly rejects citing 'current'/'latest'. Explains periodic as an incremental dated update that adds newly released PDB entries while keeping the 2.08 hierarchy, not a new stable release. Extra is_comprehensive note is bundle-supported. All must_include met. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Lineage (a / a.47 STAT-like / a.47.2 / a.47.2.1), sunids and protein/species nodes for all three structures are correct, and the fold-vs-superfamily homology distinction and no-function-transfer limits are well stated. But the answer never retrieved the domain annotations, so it omits the 'three-helical fragment; similar to one spectrin repeat' comment and the 'ms' heterogeneity flag that are the decisive evidence for a fragment-driven resemblance resolved by the full domain. Describes the full domain as a three-helix bundle without noting the missing secondary structure. Hard ceiling for ignoring the fragment annotation caps biological reasoning at 2.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Verified nodes c.2, c.2.1, c.3.1, c.4.1, c.66.1 and d.58.20 match the bundle. Frames convergence as best explanation across folds but explicitly flags the c.2/c.3/c.4 relationship as unsettled and concludes 'convergence, or at best unproven relatedness', so the caveat is present. Divergence within c.2.1, fold-vs-superfamily semantics, integrated evidence and transfer limits all covered. Minor: the periodic-update label is not in the cited bundle, and calling d.58 an 'α/β-plait-type' fold uses CATH-style naming for SCOPe's ferredoxin-like fold; neither is material.

Correct release change: 2.04 different folds (b.23.2 vs b.18.1), 2.08 same superfamily b.18.1 different families b.18.1.36/b.18.1.3, family 267607. Describes structure-discovered remote homology with topology/strand-order match and divergent binding function, caveats on no function or sequence-template transfer. Complete.

Bundle has only resolve responses; claims about K52E/L16A mutants, NMR denatured state, and d1ztra2 A:-1 to -1 in l.1.1.1 are not supported by any cited evidence. Did not query annotations, then misreads hf as 'not a clean single-chain domain example' and states 'even though the fold is shared', missing the heterogeneous-fold meaning and violating the must_avoid. Homology retained and leakage/representative-selection advice is reasonable. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Reasoning sound and adds a useful redundancy point (multiple tissue factor T:107-205 entries, supported by search results). Homology retained; align on core, trim to shared region; complete domain preferred, fragment only if best for a specific protein and said so; diversity at protein/species level; no function transfer. But it only used search/resolve endpoints and could not confirm the fr flag or its one-third definition (admitted). Protein names, protein sunids 110060/49267, family sunid 49266 and TaxId 9606 are asserted but absent from its bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation; family asserts clear homology to the superfamily and requires motif/functional/intermediate-sequence evidence; new superfamily is a conservative, falsifiable hypothesis that does not deny shared ancestry; new fold only for genuinely different arrangement/connectivity, minor variations stay within fold; rejects transfer of function/mechanism/templates and treats Dali/TM-align hits as insufficient. Release 2.08 with periodic update 2026-08-16 supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

All three families correctly placed under d.144.1 / d.144 / class d in 2.08; APH protein nodes (kanamycin kinase, type IIIa) and the PI3K helical domain a.118.1.6 are supported by the bundle. States remote homology and shared ATP-cleft phosphotransfer mechanism, explicitly rejects substrate, regulation, inhibitor and template transfer, and lists alignment of catalytic/specificity residues, biochemistry, substrate-bound structures, domain architecture/regulatory subunits, phylogeny and in-cell evidence. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
